ledger_binding.body_hash_rule: sha256 of canonical JSON of body (atlas_common.content_hash)
ledger_binding.artifact_matches_this_build_statement: artifact_matches_this_build is false because the atlas row is its own build of ssh (configure with a different line, then `make ssh`) while the closures analyse the closure trees under court/tmp/openssh-closure/{client,server}-b76; the row's recorded digest c8723f3494a2 is not the analysed binary. The field is not the per-artefact binding. Per-artefact binding is carried by the rebind receipt in evidence/sshd-artifact-ledger-b76-rebind.json and by the freeze digests recorded here, not by that field. The rebind receipt replaces only this binding with true (its ledger_record artifact_matches_this_build=true) after all eight checks pass; that replacement does not change any count, verdict or refusal, and it is not a claim that the atlas row measured the analysed binary.

per_artefact_rebind.witness: the same OpenSSH 9.9p1 recipe/source row that names ssh also built the analysed sshd: FREEZE-b76 records artefacts.files.sshd.sha256 = 547c0d14d0fed0b38f0165af1f9c65cd86309a572cdbd30abbc1d8b7c89d2a1d, the exact binary the b76c receipt analysed at court/tmp/openssh-closure/server-b76/openssh-9.9p1/sshd, whose runpath resolves libcrypto.so.3 to the freeze-proven install 8f18871713a80cc58babcd2f539f273fe9a88807acfa15bb165fb4c8fc1f4aef. Unlike b73, the atlas row was NOT rewritten to carry ssh: it still records artifact_rel='ssh' artifact_sha256=c8723f3494a2d8ea2c43bd786cf4ded342dbbb0177ded2b567d198084ef30e57, its own build (configure with a different line, then `make ssh`). This ledger is therefore the per-artefact join for sshd; it does not claim the atlas row measured sshd, and the ssh closure is bound by the freeze-proven ssh digest 0384f983b392b450a135b960c7b8f991636d509bf9ef5ff841e3d3b7367545d4 instead.

gates.verdict: fmt PASS, clippy PASS, library tests PASS serially (2304 passed, 0 failed, 54 ignored) but FAIL at --test-threads=4 under the court's default per-process RLIMIT_DATA of 4 GiB (2288 passed, 16 failed, 54 ignored). The 16 failures are all secure-heap init mmap failures (`init(1048576,16) returned 0`) and are not reproduced serially or at RLIMIT_DATA=8 GiB (diagnostic: 2304 passed, 0 failed, 54 ignored), so they are a venue limit artefact, not a source change. No test was modified and none was ignored to obtain either result.

memory.deviation: AGENTS.md section 6.1 requires host `available` >= 24 GiB before a build and a cap of min(8g, available-16g) with a 2g floor. Measured host available was 15-18 GiB throughout, so that formula yields less than 2g and the literal procedure refuses to run. This work instead ran inside an existing docker court whose cgroup hard cap is 7 GiB (memory.max=7516192768) with no swap (memory.swap.max=0), so host exposure is bounded by that cgroup. The deviation is recorded here rather than claimed as compliance.
memory.peak_note: memory.peak is the cgroup's historical high-water (raised by an earlier build), not this gate's own peak; it did not move across the three gates, and the OOM counters stayed 0 (memory.events above).
